scope: Actual loopback sockets plus real Python HTTP/service/codec/engine/Parking composition; native front and checkpoint store are synthetic fixtures.
checks: All six retained p199 outputs replay through SSE and nonstream routes with exact rendered input IDs, output text, finish reason and usage.
SAVE/RELEASE gate fixtures show content received before disposition and finish/DONE only after the acknowledgement; both policy paths covered.
Arbitrary byte-split Unicode produces monotonic stable text prefixes and preserves raw token usage including terminal ID.
Ambiguous native SAVE fixture halts service/engine intake, emits no terminal/DONE, and next HTTP request receives503 without another RUN.
Peer reset during synthetic RUN still allows complete normal SAVE or RELEASE with no pending reply and no poisoned intake.
Each test joins its serial handler; no model/native process is created.
limitations: Recorded token replay is not new generation, model correctness, latency or device evidence.
The synthetic front identity is explicitly constructed for the real codec; it does not admit the vocabulary16 native fixture to the production service.
Future HOST_ONLY probe must retain a distinct fixture-only facade and synthetic identity; production StreamingChatService compatibility remains separate.
No production lifecycle/coordinator admission is established by these socket fixtures.
